Question
========
Two studies report different average incomes. Which explanation is responsible?

Answerlist
----------
* different analysis methods
* different populations sampled
* different measurement procedures
* any of the above


Solution
========
Any of three reasons mentioned could explain why two studies report different average incomes.
*Different analysis methods* – e.g., one study uses the mean (average) while another uses the median, or they treat outliers differently. 
*Different populations sampled* – e.g., one study surveys university graduates while another surveys the entire population. 
*Different measurement procedures* – e.g., one asks for monthly income, another uses annual income, or they collect data in different ways.
It can also be a combination of two of three factors.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* False
* False
* True
